newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan OKs An Feng-Kingstream merger transaction.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan OKs An Feng-Kingstream merger transaction.

text.p: Taiwan's economic ministry said on Tuesday it had approved the purchase of a stake in An Feng Steel Co Ltd of Kaohsiung by merger partner Kingstream Resources Nl of Australia.
The ministry's Investment Commission issued a statement saying it had approved a proposal under which Kingstream had sought to buy US$582.33 million in An Feng equity.

An Feng, for its part, is taking an 80 percent stake in Kingstream to complete the deal, announced in January, in which they would merge to jointly undertake a A$1.4 billion iron and steel project in Western Australia.
The merged company, An Feng-Kingstream, would be based in Perth and have combined assets of more than A$1 billion.
Executives of An Feng, Taiwan's second-largest steelmaker, said the approval was the final regulatory hurdle on the Taiwan side to the proposed merger.
Kingstream said in March that it had reached an agreement with Western Australia state providing assurances for the huge project, to be called Midwest Iron and Steel.
The agreement with Western Australia obliged the merged company to submit detailed proposals for the project by the end of 1998, Kingstream said.
An Feng executives reached by telephone in Kaohsiung said they were not aware of other regulatory issues in Australia.
"We've checked with Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission and as far as we understand there are no further requirements," An Feng vice president Sun Kuang-tsai said.
"There should not be any problems on the Australian side," Sun added.
